back: Studying the current system in detail, identifying problems and requirements, and considering alternative solutions.
Document listing exactly what the new system must do (functional) and the qualities it must have (non-functional).
Functional: what the system does (record loans, print lists). Non-functional: qualities such as speed, security, reliability.
External entity: rectangle. Process: rounded rectangle or circle. Data store: open-ended rectangle. Data flow: labelled arrow.
Every flow is labelled and passes through a process; no flows directly between entities, between stores, or from store to entity.
Initial node: solid circle. Action: rounded rectangle. Decision/merge: diamond. Fork/join: thick bar. Final node: bullseye.
DFD: what data moves and where it is stored. Activity diagram: order of actions, decisions and parallel steps.
Improve the manual system; buy an off-the-shelf package; customise a package; have a bespoke system written.
